feature: Choosing Ask's model, and setting it up on the first Ask
summary: Nothing downloads until you want Ask. The first Ask opens one dialog that offers the right model set for this Mac, downloads it and then runs what you typed; a 16 to 32 GB Mac now gets Qwen3.5 9B, a basic model marked as basic. Settings > Ask lists every model with what it needs and its measured quality and speed, with Download, Use and Delete.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. To see a Mac with no model, move the Models folder aside: ~/Library/Application Support/Photonz/Models.

try.do: With no model on the Mac, press Ask, type a request and press Return.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Not Now: your words stay in the field and nothing downloads.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Return again, then Download: when it is done the request runs without typing it again.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: On a 16 GB Mac (walk ask-settings-lists-models-walk), press Ask and Return: the dialog offers Qwen3.5 9B, 6.6 GB.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In the dialog, press Other Models…: Settings opens at the Ask section; Qwen3.5 9B offers Download, the big ones say Too big, the weak ones Too weak.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Hover the Quality and Speed dots on a row to read the measured numbers behind them.
With two models down, press Use on the other one, then Delete and Delete 21.0 GB on the one in use.
Check Ask falls back to the model left (In Use moves to it) and the deleted one offers Download again.

evaluate: Does the setup dialog tell you enough (what Ask is, what it will download, how much room it takes) to press Download without opening Settings?
Are five dots for quality and speed, with the real numbers on hover, the right amount of detail on each row?
On a 16 to 32 GB Mac the dialog now offers Qwen3.5 9B, rated 2 of 5 for quality and for speed (about 90 s a request). Is a basic Ask marked as basic better than no Ask at all on those Macs?
Is Delete confirming in the row (Cancel, Delete 21.0 GB) clear enough, compared with a separate alert?
Should models too weak for Ask stay listed (marked Too weak for Ask) or be hidden?
An 8 GB Mac is still told it does not have enough memory: the only model that fits scored 4.6. Is that the right answer for now?
rough: An 8 GB Mac gets no model: the only one that fits it, Gemma 4 E2B, scored 4.6 held-out against the floor of 20 (Qwen3.5 4B, 12.4, reads 7.8 GB). Its row says Too weak for Ask and the dialog says the memory is short, as the task's own item allows when a size cannot do Ask's work.

Qwen3.5 9B clears the floor only just: 20.7 run as a 16 GB Mac (32k window) and 21.2 at a 64k window, so on a 16 GB Mac Ask is basic: video and simple marks work far better than drawings and layouts. Its speed was measured on an M4 Max; a base 16 GB Mac will be slower than the 92 s shown.

The 16 GB Mac's dialog does not show the quality dots, only the model's name and size; the dots and the Basic line are in Settings > Ask. Chose that over adding ratings to the dialog to keep it to one decision.
No mock page covers Settings > Ask or the setup dialog; both follow the macOS Settings row pattern (name, one line, details, trailing buttons) and a plain macOS sheet.
Delete confirms in its row rather than in an alert: a walk could not press an alert's button, nor a red destructive-role button in the row, so the confirming button is a plain one.

The setup dialog's pictures were taken with the window behind another app (no blue default button). The fresh-install picture shows Ask open with words typed and no dialog: the models folder held 0 KB before and after, and no model helper was running.

ratings.note: run as a 16 GB Mac (--mac 16, 32k window), peak memory 10.1 GB; at 64k it scored 21.2 at 76.3 s (20261102-023538-ask-held-out, first misread as 19.8 with three cases unrun)
held-out total with it on, 35.9 without

howRated: Quality is the held-out eval total (Scripts/ask-eval.sh, 45 cases, judged in total only): 1 under 20, 2 from 20, 3 from 35, 4 from 50, 5 from 60. Speed is the median seconds from Send to a result over that run: 5 at or under 20 s, 4 at or under 45, 3 at or under 90, 2 at or under 180, else 1. Under 20 a model cannot do Ask's work and is marked, never offered. All on an M4 Max, 64 GB; the small models alone on the probe with no picture model (--models), as the Macs they are for would run them; Qwen3.5 9B also planned as a 16 GB Mac (--mac 16).

macs.gets: Qwen3.5 9B, 6.6 GB (the picture model would need 22.1 GB beside it, 20.6 allowed)

freshInstall: ask-fresh-install-downloads-nothing-walk on an empty models folder: 0 KB before launch (folder absent), 0 KB after launch, opening Ask and typing; no llama-server or picture helper running.
